record.paper_title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
record.original_question: Let 1 <= p < infinity with p not equal to 2. Let Ep be Lp([0,1]^2) with Lebesgue measure on the square, and let Fp be the closed subspace of Ep consisting of functions that depend only on the first coordinate. Does Ep have an unconditional basis that can be split as (fn) union (gn), with the closed linear span of the fn equal to Fp, such that the unconditional constant of the subsequence (fn) is exactly the same as the unconditional constant of the full basis (fn) union (gn)?

evidence.quote: The number M is called the unconditional constant of the unconditional basis (xn).

Let Ep = Lp[0, 1]^2 be the Lp-space over the Lebesgue measure space of Borel subsets of the square [0, 1]^2, and let Fp be the subspace of Ep consisting of all functions depending only on the first variable.

Problem 7. Let 1 <= p < infinity, p 6= 2. Does there exist an unconditional basis (fn) union (gn) in Ep consisting of two parts such that [fn] = Fp and the unconditional constant of (fn) equals the unconditional constant of the entire basis (fn) union (gn)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1 \le p < \infty$ with $p \ne 2$. A Schauder basis $(x_n)$ of a Banach space $X$ is said to be unconditional with unconditional constant $M \ge 1$ if $M$ is the smallest constant such that, for every finitely supported scalar sequence $(a_n)$ and every choice of signs $(\varepsilon_n) \in \{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$,
$$\Big\| \sum_n \varepsilon_n a_n x_n \Big\| \le M \, \Big\| \sum_n a_n x_n \Big\|.$$
Equip $[0,1]^2$ with two-dimensional Lebesgue measure and let $E_p = L^p([0,1]^2)$. Let $F_p \subset E_p$ be the closed subspace consisting of all (equivalence classes of) functions that depend only on the first coordinate; equivalently, $F_p$ is the image of $L^p([0,1])$ under the isometric embedding $f(t) \mapsto f(t_1)$.

Question: Does there exist an unconditional basis of $E_p$ that can be written as a disjoint union $(f_n) \cup (g_n)$ such that the closed linear span $[\,(f_n)\,]$ equals $F_p$, and such that the unconditional constant of the subsequence $(f_n)$ (regarded as an unconditional basis of $F_p$) is exactly equal to the unconditional constant of the full basis $(f_n) \cup (g_n)$ of $E_p$?
artifact.status_search_result: No evidence of a resolution was found. The problem is presented as one of two long-standing open problems on $L^p$-spaces, and related structural questions about unconditional bases in subspaces of $L^p$ (such as whether every complemented subspace of $L^p$ with an unconditional basis behaves canonically) remain open in the literature. No paper claiming a solution to this specific equal-unconditional-constant question was located.

status_evidence.title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 7 asks whether such a splitting unconditional basis exists with equal unconditional constants.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Unconditional basic sequences in function spaces with applications to Orlicz spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work continues to study unconditional basic sequences in function spaces, indicating the area remains active.
status_evidence.claim: Related questions on unconditional bases in Lp-type spaces are still under active investigation.
